title: Russia attacks Kyiv with drones: petrol stations hit, five injured – photos
text:
Долучайтеся до клубу УП!

Russian forces attacked Kyiv with jet-powered drones on the morning of 11 September, with strikes recorded at petrol stations in two districts and people injured.

Source: Kyiv City Military Administration; Mayor Vitali Klitschko; State Emergency Service of Ukraine in Kyiv; acting head of Naftogaz Serhii Fedorenko

Details: Strikes were recorded at petrol stations in the Dniprovskyi and Obolonskyi districts.

At 10:07, Klitschko reported a repeat strike on a petrol station in the Obolonskyi district.

Update: The State Emergency Service of Ukraine noted that as of 11:20, five people had sustained injuries in the Russian attack, including a first responder.

All fires have now been extinguished.

Acting head of Naftogaz Serhii Fedorenko confirmed that Russian jet-powered drones have now struck two more Ukrnafta filling stations in Kyiv – in the Troieshchyna district and near the Pochayna area. In Pochayna, there was a double strike.

"As soon as the air-raid warning was issued, the stations stopped operating and all employees and customers left the premises. There is no military objective behind such attacks, nor can there be. This is terror against the civilian population, against peaceful people," he stressed.

In addition, a car was damaged in the Obolonskyi district.

At 11:10, the all-clear was given.

Previously: The Air Force warned of jet-powered drones over the capital. A red alert was declared in the city and air defence systems were operational.
